dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Sandra. Good afternoon, how can I help you?
Good afternoon, and thank you for taking my call. My name is Peggy Dolan. Thank you. I need to renew a dog license, please, and I believe I have made a mess of it already.
Oh, you're fine, hon. Renewals are pretty simple. Whose dog is it, yours?

Well, I am a property manager, and the dog belongs to a tenant at eighty-four Ayrault Street. Thank you. She is away this week and asked me to handle it. Is that allowed? I was not sure whether I am the right person to do this.
Sure, we can work with that. Sounds like you're on speaker, I'm getting a little buzz on my end.
Yes, I apologize. The speaker on my phone is cracked, and it buzzes on the high notes. Thank you for your patience. If I am hard to hear, please tell me.
No, I've got you. So the dog's license from last year, do you have the old tag number or the paperwork?
That is the problem, you see. The tag is lost. The tenant said it fell off the collar sometime in January. Thank you. I thought perhaps I needed the tag number to renew, and I do not have it.
Nope, you don't need the tag to renew. We can look her up by the owner's name and address. We'll just issue a new tag. Is it under the tenant's name?
Yes, I believe so. The name is Marguerite Okafor. Is that spelled, um, O-K-A-F-O-R? I wrote it down from her text message. Thank you.
That's how I'd spell it too. Let me pull it up. [pause] Okay, I see her. Dog's name is Biscuit?

Biscuit, yes. Thank you. Now, I have a question, and please forgive me if it is a silly one. The tenant sent me a picture of the rabies certificate. Is a copy of it accepted, or do you need the original?
A copy is generally fine. Does it show the vaccination date and when it expires?
Let me look. [pause] It says, um, given in October of last year. And then a line that says valid three years. Thank you. Is that the expiration, or is that something different?
That's probably how long the vaccine is good for. So it should cover this license year. If it's a clear copy, you're all set on that.
Oh, good. Thank you. So I can send the picture. Is it by email, or do I bring it in? I was told once that it must be the paper one with the signature.
You can bring a printed copy to the counter or send it in, either way. If you print it, make sure the vet's signature and the dates are readable.
Thank you. And, forgive me, the license itself. Do I come in to get the new tag, or does it come in the mail? I am a little unsure which.
If you come in, you walk out with it. If you send things in, we mail the tag. Mailing takes a few days, naturally.
I see. Then the mailing would go to eighty-four Ayrault Street, to the tenant. Thank you. But I will be the one sending it, so is that a problem, with the name on the form being hers and not mine?
Not a problem. Just put her name as the owner and your name as the person submitting. And if I need anything, can I reach you?
Yes, please. My number is four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-one. Thank you. Did that come through? I know the speaker buzzes.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-one. Got it.
Thank you. So, just to make sure I understand. I do not need the old tag, a copy of the certificate is fine, and I may either come to the counter or send it. Is that right?
That's it exactly. Bring a clear copy of the certificate and we'll do the rest. Biscuit will be legal in no time.
Thank you so much. One more thing, and I am sorry. When you say it is a new tag, will it have the same number as the lost one, or a different number?
Could be a different number. Don't worry about it, the record will be updated under her name either way.
Oh. All right. I am still a little unsure, but I think I will understand better when I am standing at the counter. Thank you very much for your help, Sandra.
Anytime, Peggy. Have a good afternoon.
Thank you. You as well. Goodbye.
